transmission_utility: FPL / Duke Energy Florida / Tampa Electric / JEA
additional_info: 202-acre campus in Loxahatchee (Acreage area), Palm Beach County. Near Arden community, 1.8 miles from Lion Country Safari. Zoning commission approved late 2025 but Palm Beach County Commission delayed final approval to July 15 2026 due to community opposition (noise, water, traffic, environmental impact).
source: Florida Data Centers tracker, April 30, 2026: https://floridadatacenters.org/

name: Atlas Compute AI Data Center Campus (Fort Pierce)
transmission_utility: FPL / Duke Energy Florida / Tampa Electric / JEA
additional_info: Fort Pierce, St. Lucie County. 240 MW initial capacity, expansion to 1 GW. Liquid-cooled, AI-optimized, closed-loop water-free cooling. Nearby Duke Energy Hines complex for high-capacity power.

name: Cielo Digital Infrastructure Polk County Campus
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Florida
additional_info: 74-acre campus in Polk County. Multiple high-density data center buildings. Zoning approval (PUD) secured. Fort Meade City Commission delayed final development approvals as of early 2026 due to local opposition. Adjacent to Duke Energy Hines complex.
source: Blackridge Research FL, March 24, 2026: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-top-largest-upcoming-data-center-projects-florida-usa

name: Fort Meade Data Center Complex
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Florida
additional_info: 4.4M sqft complex on former phosphate land, Fort Meade (population 5,300). Approved by Fort Meade City Commission April 15 2026. $2.6B investment.
source: Florida Data Centers tracker, April 30, 2026: https://floridadatacenters.org/

name: Lambda Kansas City Data Center
transmission_utility: Associated Electric Cooperative
additional_info: Repurposed existing unoccupied 2009-built facility in Kansas City. 100 MW planned. Announced December 2025.
source: Data Center Knowledge Dec 2025: https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/new-data-center-developments-december-2025

name: Cielo Digital Infrastructure Jackson County Campus
transmission_utility: Evergy
additional_info: ~146-acre site in Jackson County. 500 MW planned capacity. Multi-phase campus for cloud and AI workloads. Utility-scale power integration and modern cooling systems.
source: Blackridge Research MO, March 31, 2026: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-new-ai-proposed-upcoming-data-center-projects-missouri-usa

name: Cloverleaf Infrastructure Troy Data Center Campus
transmission_utility: Ameren Missouri
additional_info: 250-300 acres near St. Louis (Troy area). Up to 500 MW at full buildout. Multiple data center buildings. Part of Missouri secondary market emergence driven by central US location and fiber connectivity.
source: Blackridge Research MO, March 31, 2026: https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/latest-list-new-ai-proposed-upcoming-data-center-projects-missouri-usa

name: Metrobloks Liberty Data Center Campus
transmission_utility: Evergy
additional_info: AI-ready campus in Liberty, Clay County. Announced March 2026. MW capacity not disclosed.
source: Missouri Department of Economic Development, March 24, 2026: https://ded.mo.gov/press-room/metrobloks-announces-plans-14-billion-data-center-liberty | City of Liberty press release, March 24, 2026: https://www.libertymissouri.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/5426

name: Amazon Web Services Hinds County Campus
transmission_utility: Entergy Mississippi / Mississippi Power (Southern Company)
additional_info: Part of AWS expansion of Mississippi investment to $25B. Additional campus in Hinds County alongside Madison County Project Atlas campus. Announced May 2026.
source: Data Center Knowledge May 2026: https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/new-data-center-developments-may-2026

name: Social Circle Data Center Complex
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: 450-acre data center complex in Social Circle, Walton County GA. Cleared zoning as of May 2026 per STRisker newsletter. Developer identity not publicly disclosed.
source: STRisker Data Centers Briefing, May 7, 2026: https://writing.strisker.com/data-centers-weekly-briefing-may-4-7-2026/

name: Prince William Digital Gateway
transmission_utility: Dominion Energy / Appalachian Power / NOVEC / REC
additional_info: 2,100-acre data center corridor with 37 planned data centers (~22M sqft), billed as largest in the world. Rezoned Dec 2023. Virginia Court of Appeals struck down rezoning in March 2026 citing inadequate public notice. Prince William County Board voted April 7, 2026 not to appeal — effectively cancelling the project. Adjacent to Manassas National Battlefield Park. American Battlefield Trust filed amicus brief in support of opposition. Three separate lawsuits filed by Oak Valley Homeowners Association and others.
source: Virginia Mercury, April 8, 2026: https://virginiamercury.com/briefs/va-court-of-appeals-stops-major-data-center-development-in-prince-william-county/ | Virginia Mercury, April 24, 2026: https://virginiamercury.com/2026/04/24/local-governments-race-to-attract-data-centers-often-in-spite-of-concerns-from-their-constituents/

name: Pittsylvania County Data Center (undisclosed)
transmission_utility: Dominion Energy / Appalachian Power / NOVEC / REC
additional_info: Proposed data center project in Pittsylvania County. Community pushback and SELC-commissioned health impact report (re: on-site fossil fuel generation) led to Board of Supervisors rejecting rezoning application — project effectively killed. Cited as case study in Virginia Mercury May 2025 national opposition report.
source: Virginia Mercury, May 21, 2025: https://virginiamercury.com/2025/05/21/report-highlights-community-pushback-stalling-64-billion-in-data-center-development-nationwide/

name: Chesapeake Data Center (undisclosed)
transmission_utility: Dominion Energy / Appalachian Power / NOVEC / REC
additional_info: Rezoning proposal rejected by Chesapeake City Council following environmental and residential disruption concerns from residents. Date approximate late 2025.
source: Virginia Mercury, June 20, 2025: https://virginiamercury.com/2025/06/20/virginia-doesnt-have-statewide-data-center-regulations-localities-are-making-their-own-rules-instead/

name: Amazon King George Data Center
transmission_utility: Dominion Energy / Appalachian Power / NOVEC / REC
additional_info: $6B project initially approved Dec 2023 with performance agreement and tax abatement. New Board of Supervisors (elected 2023) voted to renegotiate. March 2024: Board Chair Collins declared county "ready to go to war." April 2024: Board voted to rezone 500+ acres back to agricultural use. Negotiations ongoing as of 2025 per Data Center Watch.
source: Data Center Watch (2025): https://www.datacenterwatch.org/report

name: Pine Ridge Technology Park (Eagle Rock Partners)
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: ~300 acres of timberland, Dry Branch area, Twiggs County. Rezoned by county commissioners mid-September 2025 despite widespread community opposition. DRI review had been paused during consideration. Lawsuit filed by county residents (led by Nancy Lubeck) seeking to overturn approval; alleges county violated its own ordinances and commissioners abused police and zoning powers. County filed December 2025 response denying claims. Project details (sqft, MW) not publicly disclosed.
source: Georgia Recorder, January 6, 2026: https://georgiarecorder.com/2026/01/06/data-center-gold-rush-pits-local-officials-hunt-for-new-revenue-against-residents-concerns/ | AJC, January 17, 2026: https://www.ajc.com/business/2025/12/why-big-tech-sees-georgia-farmland-is-ripe-for-data-centers/

name: DeKalb County Ellenwood Data Center (undisclosed)
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: Proposed 1M sqft data center in Ellenwood. DeKalb County extended moratorium on data center applications until June 2026 and deferred proposed regulations to allow further study. Proposed regulations would reclassify data centers from "minor" to "campus" facilities requiring special land-use permits restricted to industrial zones.
source: Georgia Recorder, January 6, 2026: https://georgiarecorder.com/2026/01/06/data-center-gold-rush-pits-local-officials-hunt-for-new-revenue-against-residents-concerns/

name: Trammell Crow Lamar County Technology Campus
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: 1,632-acre site along I-75 approximately 60 miles southeast of downtown Atlanta. $21B technology campus. Planning and rezoning process in early stages as of late 2025. Near Barnesville.
source: AJC, November 28, 2025: https://www.ajc.com/business/2025/11/21b-data-center-proposal-aims-to-become-one-of-georgias-largest/

name: Wallace Jackson Data Center Campus
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: 10 data center buildings, nearly 5M sqft — more than three Lenox Square malls. State infrastructure (DRI) filing submitted early January 2026. Developer not publicly identified. Located in Spalding County (Griffin area).

name: Amazon Web Services Rock House Road Campus
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: 118-acre undeveloped land along Rock House Road near Douglas/Cobb county border. Paid $37M+. Rezoning application seeking ~4.2M sqft across 12 buildings along Rumble Road. Build-out value ~$1.1B. 30-50 full-time employees. Rezoning before Douglas County as of late 2025.
source: AJC, October 15, 2024: https://www.ajc.com/news/business/a-proposed-data-center-near-macon-would-be-larger-than-the-mall-of-georgia/QIOM5PHZ4FAH5OS2HHOGB4VDPI/

name: Datacore Bibb County (Macon) Data Center
transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: Rezoning application for ~4.2M sqft across 12 buildings along Rumble Road, Bibb County. Build-out value ~$1.1B. 30-50 full-time jobs. Developer argues site will preserve more green space than standard industrial. Application active as of late 2024/early 2025. "Larger than the Mall of Georgia."
source: AJC, October 15, 2024: https://www.ajc.com/news/business/a-proposed-data-center-near-macon-would-be-larger-than-the-mall-of-georgia/QIOM5PHZ4FAH5OS2HHOGB4VDPI/

transmission_utility: Georgia Power (Southern Company) / Georgia Transmission Corp
additional_info: $10B project on site in Butts County. Rezoning application before planning commission December 2025; county commission to consider beginning January 2026. Significant political controversy: Lt. Gov. Burt Jones accused by GA Attorney General Chris Carr of using office for family financial benefit. Jones family tied to development. Billboard paid for by Keep Georgia Strong Action Inc. (Carr-aligned group).
source: Georgia Recorder, December 1, 2025: https://georgiarecorder.com/2025/12/01/massive-burt-jones-backed-project-among-wave-of-data-centers-proposed-for-georgia/

name: Natelli Investments Henderson Data Center Campus
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Duke Energy Progress
additional_info: 250 MW campus in Henderson, Vance County. Rezoning approved May 2026. Separate citizen petition with 370+ signatures calling for county-wide one-year moratorium on data centers pending new policies. Note: Natelli withdrew a separate 250 MW application in Apex, NC (Wake County) after community opposition — the Henderson (Vance County) site is proceeding. Developer linked to Natelli Communities (southeastern US residential/commercial developer).
source: Data Center Dynamics, April 2026: https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/officials-in-north-carolina-county-give-ok-for-rezoning-potential-data-center-incoming/

name: Charlotte Data Center Moratorium (proposed)
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Duke Energy Progress
additional_info: Charlotte City Council voted May 12, 2026 to schedule May 26 public hearing on a proposed 150-day data center moratorium. Formal vote expected June 8, 2026. Data centers currently allowed by right in 8 zoning districts including residential. NC Senate Bill 382 (2024) restricts downzoning, complicating options. All existing facilities within 500 feet of homes. Moratorium driven by rezoning-process concerns.
source: STRisker Data Centers Daily Notes, May 12, 2026: https://writing.strisker.com/data-centers-daily-notes-may-12-2026/

name: Natelli Apex Data Center (withdrawn)
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Duke Energy Progress
additional_info: 250 MW data center campus proposed in Apex, Wake County. Natelli withdrew application following opposition from residents and local government. Withdrawn approximately April 2026.

name: Franklin (Simpson County) AI Data Center
transmission_utility: East Kentucky Power / Big Sandy RECC
additional_info: Proposed AI data center off I-65 in Franklin, Simpson County. Simpson County ordinance requiring conditional use permit for data centers currently being challenged by developer. Residents protested Oct 21, 2025 at Planning and Zoning Commission meeting. Developer linked to New York-based Western Hospitality Partners, which also withdrew from a Kentucky project after community opposition elsewhere. (Note: Western Hospitality Partners also pulled back from Pekin, IL.)
source: WKMS/LPM, May 12, 2026: https://www.wkms.org/government-politics/2026-05-12/a-data-center-insider-wants-to-halt-their-construction-in-kentucky

name: Cave City (Barren County) Data Center (blocked)
transmission_utility: East Kentucky Power / Big Sandy RECC
additional_info: Barren County Joint City-County Planning Commission declined to amend zoning regulations for Cave City and approved a one-year moratorium on data center development as of May 2026. Developer identity not disclosed.
source: WKMS/LPM, May 12, 2026: https://www.wkms.org/government-politics/2026-05-12/a-data-center-insider-wants-to-halt-their-construction-in-kentucky

transmission_utility: Entergy Mississippi / Mississippi Power (Southern Company)
additional_info: 648-acre site in Clarksdale between Sunflower River, U.S. 278, Tallahatchie Street and the Roundyard neighborhood. Rezoned March 24, 2026 by Clarksdale Board of Commissioners (3-0) with conditions: $5M one-time impact fee, developer pays public utility improvements, 1,000-foot residential setback. Developer described as "global company" by city officials but identity not disclosed. No signed agreements as of vote. Community divided — many see economic benefits for struggling Delta city. Economic development org: Crossroads Economic Partnership (Coahoma County).

name: PraCon Global Ridgeland AI Campus
transmission_utility: Entergy Mississippi / Mississippi Power (Southern Company)
additional_info: Ridgeland/Madison County. Developer filed request for declaratory opinion with Mississippi PSC on April 22, 2026 seeking to self-generate electricity for AI and semiconductor facilities. Entergy Mississippi and Mississippi Power filed opposition April 13, 2026 arguing self-generation would make PraCon a public utility. PSC asked Public Utilities Staff for input by May 15; will issue opinion by June 1, 2026. Multiple AI campuses possible across Mississippi. Investors and tenants in discussions but undisclosed. CEO: Gabriel Prado.
source: Mississippi Today, April 22, 2026: https://mississippitoday.org/2026/04/22/ridgeland-data-center-entergy-mississippi-power/

name: Amazon Web Services Canton Data Center (Madison County)
transmission_utility: Entergy Mississippi / Mississippi Power (Southern Company)
additional_info: Under construction as of October 2025 in Canton, Madison County. Part of AWS Madison County campus (Project Atlas). Confirmed under construction by Mississippi Today satellite/site visit October 4, 2025.
source: Mississippi Today, November 20, 2025: https://mississippitoday.org/2025/11/20/amazon-data-center-warren-county-mississippi/

name: Hoover Data Center Review Ordinance
transmission_utility: Alabama Power (Southern Company) / PowerSouth
additional_info: Hoover City Council approved ordinance creating case-by-case review process for future data center proposals. Date: May 12, 2026.

name: Google Midlothian Data Center Campus
transmission_utility: Oncor
additional_info: One of three data centers announced as part of Google Cloud $40B Texas investment over two years (Nov 14, 2025). Google CEO Sundar Pichai joined Gov. Abbott in Midlothian for announcement. Companion campuses in Armstrong and Haskell counties (West Texas/Panhandle). Midlothian in Ellis County south of Dallas-Fort Worth.
source: Texas Tribune, November 14, 2025: https://www.texastribune.org/2025/11/14/texas-google-data-centers-ai/

name: San Marcos AI Data Center (undisclosed, rejected)
transmission_utility: Oncor

source: Texas Tribune, May 7, 2026: https://www.texastribune.org/2026/05/07/texas-republicans-data-centers-rural/

name: Compass Datacenters Red Oak Campus 2
transmission_utility: Oncor
additional_info: 830-acre second campus in Red Oak, Ellis County. Rezoning from agricultural to planned development approved by Red Oak City Council May 12, 2026. Tax abatement also approved (same vote). Every resident who spoke in public comment opposed the rezoning. Nearly five-hour meeting.
source: STRisker Data Centers Daily Notes, May 12, 2026: https://writing.strisker.com/data-centers-daily-notes-may-12-2026/

name: Conway Data Center (undisclosed Fortune 100)
transmission_utility: Entergy Arkansas / SWEPCO
additional_info: Site near Lollie Road, Conway, Faulkner County. 333 acres annexed and rezoned to heavy industrial (Planning Commission 6-4 vote, Little Rock Board of Directors approved days later). Additional 160 acres also rezoned. No building permits issued as of mid-2025. Developer is a Fortune 100 company but identity not disclosed. Separately, 783 acres near Port of Little Rock rezoned to heavy industrial for a second unnamed data center and recent Amazon announcement. City ordinance requires noise study and attenuation plan with conditional use permit.
source: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, August 1, 2025: https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2025/aug/01/central-arkansas-data-center-projects-not/ | Talk Business & Politics, January 12, 2026: https://talkbusiness.net/2026/01/6-billion-data-center-to-locate-near-little-rock/

name: Marion County Data Center (undisclosed)
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Dominion Energy SC / Santee Cooper
additional_info: $2.4B data center approved by Marion County Council on January 22, 2026, during a major winter storm when most residents were unaware of the meeting. Community members criticized the speed and secrecy of the process. Developer identity not publicly disclosed. Majority-Black rural county. Capital B News reported project came shortly after developers failed to site a similar complex in a predominantly white community, before relocating interest to Marion County.
source: Capital B News, February 4, 2026: https://capitalbnews.org/secret-data-center-deal-marion-county-south-carolina/

name: Eagle Rock Partners Colleton County Data Center
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Dominion Energy SC / Santee Cooper
additional_info: Proposed data center complex in Colleton County (majority-Black rural county). Preceded by failed attempt to site the same project in a predominantly white rural community where residents organized fierce opposition and filed lawsuits. Southern Environmental Law Center filed lawsuit to block a zoning ordinance passed to accommodate the project, arguing it opens rural SC to industrial development. Similar ordinances have been passed across GA and LA.
source: Capital B News, February 4, 2026: https://capitalbnews.org/secret-data-center-deal-marion-county-south-carolina/

name: Google Dorchester County Ridgeville Campus (Project Dawson)
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Dominion Energy SC / Santee Cooper
additional_info: First of two new Google campuses in Dorchester County. 230-acre site at Pine Hill Business Campus, Ridgeville. Google originally filed as Project Dawson / Mallard LLC. Broke ground September 2024. Part of Google $3.3B SC investment announced September 2024, expanded to $9B two-year investment announced October 13, 2025. Also covers existing Berkeley County campus expansion and second Dorchester County campus (St. George). Entergy and Duke Energy Carolinas provide power.
source: Google / Dorchester County Fact Sheet: https://www.dorchestercountysc.gov/business/data-center-fact-sheet | Data Center Dynamics, May 2026: https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/google-to-invest-9bn-in-south-carolina-data-centers/
address: 1055 Research Center Drive, Ridgeville, SC (Pine Hill Business Campus)

name: Google Dorchester County St. George Campus (Project Evergreen)
transmission_utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Dominion Energy SC / Santee Cooper
additional_info: Second of two new Google campuses in Dorchester County. 206-acre site in Winding Woods Commerce Park, St. George (approx. 18 miles west of Ridgeville). Google originally filed as Project Evergreen / Gannett Enterprises LLC. Broke ground September 2024. Part of $9B Google South Carolina investment announced October 2025.
source: Google / Dorchester County Fact Sheet: https://www.dorchestercountysc.gov/business/data-center-fact-sheet | Data Center Dynamics, May 2026: https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/google-to-invest-9bn-in-south-carolina-data-centers/
address: Winding Woods Commerce Park, St. George, SC

name: Google Project Pyramid (West Memphis)
transmission_utility: Entergy Arkansas
additional_info: 1,178-acre site; 5 data center buildings + office space + on-site substation across ~580 acres. Largest private investment in Arkansas history. Groundbreaking ceremony October 2025 with Gov. Sanders. Google to invest $4B through 2027. 300 permanent jobs, 5,000+ construction jobs. Property tax revenue ~$120M for local schools. APSC approved 600 MW solar + 350 MW battery storage (Entergy Arkansas) October 2025. Google $25M Energy Impact Fund for Crittenden County affordability. Demand-response "load flexibility" contract with Entergy. Google confirmed September 2025 after operating under Groot LLC / Project Pyramid codename.

name: Mason County Hyperscale Campus (Fortune 50, undisclosed)
transmission_utility: East Kentucky Power Cooperative
